script.analysis: All 17,717 stored characters read in three contiguous ranges with canonical hash match. Hook: second-person drift after payoff, "$600,000 or $0" stake; subscribe CTA. Composite Karen (54, Columbus HR, bought 2001 for $187K, final $1,940 payment). Mechanisms: arrival fallacy (Ben-Shahar), licensing effect, month-by-month creep (car lease $340, financed bathroom $490, gym, cable, vacation on card). Projection $1,940/month at 8% for 13 years = $529K. Fix: automate the transfer on the old due date; hierarchy (emergency fund in HYSA, high-interest debt, 401k catch-up, Roth IRA, taxable index fund); self-managed escrow ($3,600 taxes + $1,800 insurance + 1% maintenance on $310K = ~$700); HELOC-to-invest warning. Ideal-Karen allocation and $450K-$550K outcome; margin/choice close; like/subscribe and comment CTA. Clear practical structure with a running character and concrete numbers. Problems: projections use the full $1,940 although the script later says only ~$1,240 is genuinely available, final plan exceeds available cash, and contribution limits are 2025 values in a March 2026 video. ASR glitch ("leaving for doing the table for doing nothing") preserved; not audio-verified.

claim_audit: 0:7000 $1,940/month at 8% monthly compounding for 13 years = ~$529,466 and contributions 1,940 x 156 = $302,640, both correct. Hook "$1,500-$2,200 freed payment -> $600,000": at 8% for 13 years $1,500 gives ~$409K and $2,200 gives ~$600K, so $600K is the top of the range, not "typical". "Median freed mortgage payment" unsourced. $8,400 over 18 months is $467 at 0%; $490 implies financing cost, plausible. Arrival fallacy correctly attributed to Tal Ben-Shahar; licensing effect is an established concept applied loosely.

7000:14000 401k limits stated as $23,500 base + $7,500 catch-up = $31,000 and Roth IRA $8,000 for 50+ are 2025 figures; for 2026 the IRS limits are $24,500 + $8,000 catch-up = $32,500 and $7,500 + $1,100 = $8,600 IRA for 50+. Roth phase-out ends stated as $165K single / $246K MFJ match 2025 upper bounds, not 2026. $666/month at 8% for 13 years = ~$181,765, matches $182K; growth ~$78K correct. 4.0-4.2% top HYSA and 0.39% national average plausible for early 2026 but unverified here. 22% card payoff as guaranteed return is a standard framing (avoided interest).

7000:14000 Escrow: 3,600 + 1,800 + 3,100 = $8,500/year = ~$708/month, correct; 1,940 - 700 = 1,240 correct. But the October "$5,200 bill" does not match the stated $3,600 property tax (taxes + insurance = $5,400). If taxes and insurance were escrowed inside the $1,940 payment, they were never "freed", so the $529K projection overstates; $1,240/month at 8% for 13 years = ~$338K. "For 30 years" escrow conflicts with 23 years/276 payments. HELOC 7.2-7.6% and the leverage/collateral warning are reasonable.

14000:17717 Ideal-Karen plan: Roth $666 + escrow $700 + intentional $300 = $1,666 before the 401k increase (~$18K/year more, ~$1,500/month pre-tax) and a taxable account reaching "$200,000 or more", which together exceed the $1,240 truly freed (or even $1,940). "$450K-$550K total from the freed payment" therefore does not reconcile with the script's own cash constraint. Paid-off home as liquidatable insurance is reasonable but home equity is illiquid without selling or borrowing.
